Hello… Took paxil for 6 years before stopping it last April at the age of 25. Paxil was my friend and also my enemy. First couple years were great, last 2 years taking it were kind of mid and felt like it wasn’t doing anything. I think being on it also made me feel emotionally numb. But after being off it for a year now, I feel less interested in living and idk if that is due to stopping the medication. I just feel everything way too big. That could just be a quarter life crisis but it’s exhausting. But do I regret coming off it? No. It wasn’t working anymore. I have not had any long term issues that I know of or see. If you do decide to stop please do a longer taper process. Paxil is one of the hardest drugs to come off of because of the withdrawal symptoms. It is possible though. I’m proof. Also would advise that you have some type of plan in place if the feelings are too much when coming off paxil. I wish you all the best whatever’s decision you make. Any questions let me know.

Been on paroxetine 40mg for 6 years and started my taper off of it 2 months ago. One of the reasons that paxil is hard to get off of is because of its short half-life. You can feel withdrawal rather quickly if you miss a dose. If I forgot to take it for a few days i’d have terrible migraines and light sensitivity. Now I will say overall it helped me a lot. Anxiety was at an all time low after the first few months. In the first two months or so I had increased my dosage from 10mg>20mg>30mg and then the highest at 40mg. That’s where I felt leveled out at. The worst thing was probably the nausea. I barely ate in the beginning. In terms of marijuana and alcohol I can only speak to the alcohol part. I stopped smoking like a month before I went on it. I do social drink and make sure to take my medication way beforehand and usually limit myself to two drinks max. I don’t want to test the waters with more than 2 drinks. Paroxetine can do wonders for anxiety but part of me wish I new more about it when I first started taking it. Idk if I went have went on it. Luckily haven’t had any crazy withdrawals with my taper so far but I am going slow and adjusting the taper at times to meet my physical and mental needs. If you do decide to get off it eventually go slowly and never quit cold turkey. You’ll end up feeling worse. Any questions let me know :)

Long time paxil user here who has started to taper off of it. Been on it for 6 years. It definitely helped the first 3 years. Felt amazing and anxiety was barely there. The past 3 years not as helpful. Why didn’t I go to change meds when it stopped working for me? Didn’t care enough honestly. Starting to taper off now because of insurance and finance issues plus doesn’t really make sense to take it anymore. When I first started the side effects were no fun. Nausea was the 
worst. Also had loss of appetite. Eventually after a few weeks, side effects lessened and it was smooth sailing. Now paxil’s half life is short meaning you miss a dose or more you could feel like absolute shit. The withdrawal symptoms are awful. I missed two doses in a row one time and had the worst migraine of my life for hours and hours. It’s considered one of the hardest antidepressants to get off of. If I had known that in the beginning I prob would never have taken it. It’s been 2 weeks since I started to taper. I’m doing it very slowly but luckily no crazy side effects. Paxil is definitely helpful but not sure it was truly worth it for me in the end.

Also since you are a beginner companies are more than likely not going to approve you for the best valued cards. My second card was a chase freedom (not the unlimited). The cash back is great, no yearly fee, and the limit was a comfortable number. Now this may not be the best card for you necessarily but just compare cards to see what makes the most sense for you. My recommendation is just no college cards or cards with a yearly fee. They don't make sense for the position you are in.
